cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is traveling with his companions, and the writer of Acts is one of them. They go on ahead to the ship and sail for Assos, where they'll take Paul aboard. But Paul has arranged his own way to get to Assos.

cards.question: Paul's companions sail to Assos to take him aboard there. How is Paul getting to Assos?

answers.text: He rides there on a donkey
He sails there on another ship

cards.text: Paul meets them at Assos, and they sail on to Mitylene, then reach opposite Chios the next day, Samos the day after, and Miletus the day after that. Friend, that's not a cruise, that's a man who keeps checking the time.

cards.question: Paul decides to sail right past Ephesus so he won't spend time in the province of Asia. Why is he in such a hurry?

cards.text: From Miletus, Paul sends to Ephesus for the elders of the church, and when they come, he says they know how he lived among them: serving the Lord with great humility and with tears, even through trials from the plots of the Jews. Friend, ask the junk drawer I got stuck in for years how I lived, and it'd say, "Under a takeout menu."
Paul says, "I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you…" No "let's circle back on that next quarter."

cards.question: Paul taught the Ephesians everything that was helpful. Where did he teach them?

answers.text: Publicly and from house to house
Outdoors and down by the riverside

cards.question: While Paul was with the Ephesians, what did he testify about?

answers.text: Repentance to God and faith in Jesus
Keeping the feasts and the law
Fasting and giving to the poor

cards.question: Paul says he testified to Greeks as well as to Jews.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to what's ahead. Compelled by the Spirit, he's going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to him there, and friend, I can't even open an email called "Quick question" without bracing myself.

cards.question: In town after town, the Holy Spirit warns Paul that chains and afflictions are waiting for him.
Chains and afflictions are waiting for Paul. So what does he say matters more to him than his own life?

answers.text: Finishing the ministry Jesus gave him
Seeing his friends one more time

cards.question: Paul tells the Ephesian elders he'll come back and see them again after Jerusalem.

cards.text: Paul says he's innocent of the blood of all men. And there's that line again: "For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God."
Now Paul hands the job to the elders: keep watch over themselves and the entire flock the Holy Spirit made them overseers of. That's the church God purchased with His own blood.

cards.question: The Holy Spirit made the elders overseers of the flock. Paul also tells them to be ___ of the church of God.
Paul has been calling the church a flock. He warns that after he departs, savage ___ will come in among them and not spare the flock.

cards.text: And the danger isn't only from outside. Paul says that even from the elders' own number, men will rise up.

cards.question: Paul warns that men from the elders' own number will rise up. What will those men do?

answers.text: Distort the truth to draw disciples after them
Leave the church and go their own way
Hand the elders over to the rulers

cards.text: So be alert, Paul says, and remember that for three years he never stopped warning each of them, night and day, with tears. That is NOT a man who sent one reminder text and called it a day.

cards.question: Paul commits the Ephesian elders to God and to the word of His grace. What does Paul say can happen for them?

answers.text: They can be built up and given an inheritance
They can be kept free from every hardship
They can be given wealth and long lives

cards.text: Paul says he never coveted anyone's silver or gold or clothing. Me? I have stared at somebody else's batch of chocolate chip cookies a LITTLE too long, friend.

cards.question: Paul never wanted anyone's silver or gold. Instead, he says his own ___ took care of his needs and the needs of his companions.
Paul says hard work like his is how we must help the weak. Which words of the Lord Jesus does he remember?

answers.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive
The worker is worthy of his wages
Ask and it will be given to you

cards.text: When Paul has said all this, he kneels down with every one of them. Every single elder, right there, nobody standing in the back pretending to check their phone.

cards.question: Paul is on his knees with the Ephesian elders. What does he do?
The Ephesian elders hold back their tears as they say goodbye to Paul.

cards.text: What grieves them especially is Paul's statement that they'll never see his face again. I think that one hurts.

cards.question: The Ephesian elders have prayed and wept with Paul at Miletus. Where do they go with him next?

cards.text: Friend, Paul's road isn't finished yet, and neither is this story.
